openapi.title: WebWolf 8.2.2 surface (operator-supplied seed, extracted from bytecode)

workflows.note: state-changing surfaces grouped by target; multi-step flow learning is the Phase 58 business-logic engine

hypotheses.premise: POST /WebWolf/fileupload changes state and carries no anti-CSRF token — a hostile origin may be able to forge this action against an authenticated victim
POST /WebWolf/jwt/encode changes state and carries no anti-CSRF token — a hostile origin may be able to forge this action against an authenticated victim
POST /WebWolf/mail changes state and carries no anti-CSRF token — a hostile origin may be able to forge this action against an authenticated victim
POST /WebWolf/register.mvc changes state and carries no anti-CSRF token — a hostile origin may be able to forge this action against an authenticated victim

planner.policy: READ_ONLY/LOW_IMPACT automatic; STATE_CHANGING needs --logic-active; DESTRUCTIVE blocked

proofs.attack_hypothesis: a hostile-origin state-changing request is accepted like a same-origin one

responses.detail: state-changing POST accepted from hostile origin (https://csrf-probe.example): baseline -> HTTP 200 (5061B), cross-origin replay -> HTTP 200 (5061B) — no CSRF token in the form and no Origin/Referer validation

impact.statement: A state-changing request from a hostile origin was accepted exactly like a same-origin one (fresh-origin replay) — silent cross-site action forgery against authenticated users.
impact.safe_proof: non-destructive verification: fresh-input replay / differential oracle / marker read — no data extraction, no state change, no destructive payload

reproduction.expect: an authenticated session cookie/header

reproduction.request: send POST http://127.0.0.1:9090/WebWolf/register.mvc with the tested parameter 'username, password, matchingPassword, agree' and the canary value from the evidence chain
reproduction.expect: the same evidence kind fires as in the attached proof (cross_origin_acceptance)

verification.notes: cross-origin replay from https://csrf-vr13-7f5b07cc.example accepted: True (HTTP 200)

proofs.attack_hypothesis: an attacker-controlled Host is reflected into application output

responses.detail: canary Host reflected in location header: the application builds output from the attacker-controlled Host header (link-manipulation / reset-poisoning class). canary=sentinel-hh-b9ee6c5d47.example

impact.statement: An attacker-controlled Host header value is reflected into application output (fresh canary host) — password-reset poisoning and cache-poisoning preconditions.
impact.safe_proof: non-destructive verification: fresh-input replay / differential oracle / marker read — no data extraction, no state change, no destructive payload
